label: AQ 0053
title: The file it never looked for

questions.q: Why not fine-tune the 2B on runs that start by listing files?
questions.a: You could, but fine-tuning on one harness's runs also teaches that harness's habits, and such a model can collapse in another harness (guide 25). Harness changes are cheaper to try and travel between models: SWE-agent's interface, built for GPT-4 Turbo, still solved 10.5% of the full benchmark with Claude 3 Opus.

teach.title: How it works: four harness changes, then the model question

questions.q: How should the harness catch a fake success like this?
questions.a: Never take the agent's word. The harness runs the real verify.py itself on a clean copy plus the agent's diff, and checks that the diff edits parser.py at its original path rather than creating a new file (our design). Anthropic's SWE-bench edit tool also refuses to create a file where one already exists.

teach.title: How it works: four harness changes, then the model question

questions.q: When is the bigger model the right call?
questions.a: When the same tasks still fail in a good harness, and the traces show the agent reading the right code and still fixing it wrongly, not failing to look. Anthropic notes that SWE-bench scores vary a lot with the scaffolding even for one model, so compare models in the same harness, on cost per solved task.

teach.title: How it works: four harness changes, then the model question

questions.q: Why didn't the coding agent's own passing check catch that it never fixed the real file?
questions.a: It chose what to check: its own new copy of the file. A check means something only when the harness picks it and runs it against the real file (our reasoning).

questions.q: Name three harness changes that stop a coding agent writing its own copy of a file it was asked to fix.
questions.a: Show the folder listing at the start and ask it to read before editing; a create tool that refuses a path that already exists; and the harness, not the agent, runs the check on the real file and inspects the diff.

questions.q: Why compare a 2B and a 70B coding agent in the same harness, on cost per solved task?
questions.a: Harness changes alone move scores: SWE-agent's tools took GPT-4 Turbo from 11.0% with a plain shell to 18.0% on SWE-bench Lite. Compared in one harness, a cheaper model that solves somewhat fewer tasks can still cost far less per solved task.
